$comment: Config for the feature-delivery workflow (.claude/skills/feature-delivery/SKILL.md). The workflow never fires on its own — it runs only when invoked as /feature-delivery. This file carries the tunables and the hard off switch.

authority.$comment: Agents review and comment. A human is the sole approver. Every shipped multi-agent system researched keeps it this way, and on 2026-08-16 a ticket in this repo passed its own author's evidence and still failed independent QA — self-approval would have shipped it.

parallelism.$comment: Reads parallelise, writes do not. Spawn parallel writers only for named independent modules, each in its own worktree. Default is one implementer — 'can this split into disjoint sub-tickets?' is the real question, not 'how many devs?'.

quality.$comment: Quality outranks speed. These are not tunables — turning one off means the workflow is no longer being followed. See the 'quality bar' section of the skill.
quality.evidenceNotAssertion: Every claim must be backed by pasted command output someone else could re-run. 'The code looks right' is not verification.
quality.testsMustBeProvablyAbleToFail: Break it, watch red, restore, watch green. A test that passes whether or not the feature exists reads as coverage and is worse than none.
quality.writeTestFirstForLatentDefects: Red-then-fix is the only honest order for a bug that has not surfaced — otherwise the test merely agrees with the code.
quality.featureMustBeReachable: A correct procedure with no UI caller is not delivered (SYSTEM_PLAN.md §9). Grep for a call site and drive it in a browser.
quality.verifyTheDataNotTheScreen: Event-sourced: after any mutation query the row AND the transaction row. A green screen is a claim.
quality.adversarialQaAlwaysRequired: Every ticket, including small ones. Never risk-scaled. The verifier must be a different agent with fresh context.
quality.verifierMustTryAnUntriedInput: The habit that has caught every real failure here. Implementer evidence is usually genuine and incomplete.
quality.reportFailurePlainly: Failing tests get shown with output. Skipped steps get named. Blocked work finishes everything unblocked and states what was left.

gates.$comment: Ordered. Deterministic checks first — they are cheap and unambiguous. Review agents run only after QA passes, so they never review code that is still moving.

e2e.scope: once per phase, not per ticket

gates.$ultrareviewNote: Deep multi-agent review (/code-review ultra) is deliberately NOT a gate here. The user runs it themselves, once, after all work is complete. No agent invokes it, prompts for it, or simulates it.

review.$comment: Noise is the enemy, not missed bugs. A reviewer leaving 14 comments of which 11 are wrong is worse than no reviewer, because people learn to ignore it. These limits are the mitigation.
excludedFindingCategories: generic input validation without proven impact

sizing.$comment: No vendor publishes an agents-per-task-size rubric. This is reasoned from the reads/writes constraint, not received wisdom. Scale writers by independent modules, never by line count.

L.action: split into sub-tickets before dispatching anyone

records.$comment: Feature records are append-only archives frozen at merge, never documents kept current. Spec-and-plan files that are maintained drift, and agents then execute stale specs at machine speed. Scale the file count to ticket size.

sections: What — the change, in one paragraph
Why — the ticket link and the problem it solves
How tested — real command output and database evidence, not assertions
Deviations — where the plan turned out wrong, and why
Out of scope — adjacent problems found and their ticket references
